newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan moves to boost Asian Development Bank role.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan moves to boost Asian Development Bank role.

text.p: Taiwan's central bank said on Wednesday it and the economics ministry would host a seminar to help local firms play a greater role in projects financed by the Asian Development Bank (ADB).
The central bank was inviting ADB experts to the June 24-25 meeting in Taipei to explain bidding procedures for purchases and construction engineering for ADB projects, it said.
The ADB has pledged to increase its use of Taiwanese staff and support Taiwan firms in international bidding for contracts in ADB development projects, the central bank has said.

Taiwan is a member of the ADB -- one of the few international organisations where China tolerates its presence. China has been Taiwan's rival since the Nationalists fled to the island after losing a civil war to the Communists in 1949.
The ADB has found Taiwan's capital market attractive.
In August 1995, the ADB issued a seven-year Taiwan dollar-denominated bond valued at T$2.6 billion, or roughly US$100 million.
In a second tranche in December 1996, the ADB issued T$7 billion or US$255 million in Taiwan dollar-denominated bonds.
The central bank has hailed the ADB's bond issues for helping to internationalise Taiwan's bond market and raise the credibility of Taiwan's currency.
